thread:
Alex (Marketing): Quick sync: need a compact 1-pager + short field deck for an outbound push this sprint. Focus: security controls + SLA decision criteria across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Also want one clear benchmark stat on latency to lead with.

Maria (Product): I can assemble the deployment comparison and a short cost example. Tone? executive with a brief tech appendix?

Alex (Marketing): Exactly. Executive main panel, include an appendix slide with technical proof points (latency, batching notes, quantization). One prominent stat: p50 text-gen latency on a 2k prompt vs public competitor number. Do we have that validated?

Dave (Research): Ran microbench yesterday. p50 = 120ms on our Dedicated stack for a 2k streaming prompt. Public competitor figure we found is ~220ms. Ill export chart and write a short methodology blurb.

Sarah (Sales Ops): Field also needs a simple ROI example for sales conversations: monthly token volume scenario + estimated savings with batching/caching. Can someone draft a conservative delta we can quote?

Maria (Product): Will draft: mid-market SaaS, 50M tokens/month, estimated 20% lower per-token spend with our batching + cache profile. Will keep the math transparent.

Alex (Marketing): Nice. Also need routing triggers for inbound leads: three bullets - 1) Self-serve trial -> Hosted API; 2) High-volume threshold or SLA ask -> SDR handoff to discuss Dedicated; 3) Regulated/compliance -> Solutions Eng + Private onboarding. Keep routing triggers short.

Ben (Solutions Eng): For Private, call out KMS/HSM support, audit log retention options, and on-prem packaging. Also note assistance for network setup (VPC peering).

Design (Design): Will produce a hero that conveys both security and speed (proposal: abstract padlock + tachometer motif). Will share options in #design-review by EOD.

Ollie (Comms): We should craft two short copy pieces: 1) a launch post announcing the resource and benchmark, and 2) a webinar invite blurb titled "Choosing deployment modes for SLA-driven LLMs". Webinar: 30-40m panel + short demo.

Alex (Marketing): Yes. Put webinar callout on slide 2. Also we need a one-paragraph benchmark narrative for press/analysts with methodology summary and a short disclaimer about comparatives.

Dave (Research): Ill write the methodology note and bundle the raw CSV. Note from legal: avoid direct named comparisons unless cleared.

Priya (Legal): Legal-review-bot created BR-2024-229 for benchmark wording review. Ill review and advise; please include the methodology link and avoid unverified comparative claims.

Legal-review-bot: New request BR-2024-229 created. Owner: priya. ETA: 48h.

Sarah (Sales Ops): For SDR ops, Ill convert routing triggers into tags and an automated routing matrix: tag:deploy_mode_interest, tag:security_profile, tag:token_volume_est. Will add playbook snippets for handoffs.

Maria (Product): Assignments: product content + deploy comparison + cost example (due today 16:00).
Dave (Research): benchmark stat + methodology + chart (due today 15:00).
Design (Design): hero + slide templates (due EOD).
Ollie (Comms): launch post + webinar blurb (due tomorrow 12:00).
Sarah (Sales Ops): routing matrix + SDR playbook snippet (due tomorrow 09:00).

Ben (Solutions Eng): Ill draft a short platform checklist for the appendix (KMS, audit retention, VPC peering, cert rotations, monitoring hooks).

Alex (Marketing): Style notes for the 1-pager: front side = customer problem + 3 quick callouts (security, SLA, cost). Back side = solution highlights + routing triggers + benchmark stat. Keep total copy under ~250 words.

Maria (Product): Uploaded draft deck v0.1 -> https://drive.redwood/example/deck_v0.1.pptx

Dave (Research): Chart + methodology bundle uploaded -> https://drive.redwood/example/benchmarks.zip

Design (Design): Thumbnails posted in #design-review. Please pick top 2 by 17:00.

Ollie (Comms): Launch post draft in docs: https://docs.redwood/launch/draft feel free to comment.

Sarah (Sales Ops): Routing matrix added to SDR playbook and linked into the lead queue.

Alex (Marketing): If Legal marks the benchmark phrasing, we will switch to neutral language: "internal microbenchmarks show" with methodology link, avoid competitor names. Great work team, reconvene here if anything changes. :rocket:
